text:
Alice Chen: heads up — seeing a weird spike in kube-proxy retries for the gpu-pool svc, lots of 502/503 from the inference pods since ~08:10 UTC
Mateo Ruiz: observed same from EU-west2: gpu-pool-07 especially. p50 latency ok, p99 balloons and requests get retried to other endpoints a few times
Alice Chen: attaching quick logs (excerpt):
```
E0508 08:10:12.345 pod.go:234] 503 Service Unavailable: no healthy endpoints
2026-05-08T08:10:12Z inference: request failed: upstream reset after 2 retries
```
Priya Kapoor: can you run `ipvsadm -Ln --numeric` on kube-proxy host? want to see endpoint weights and persistent conn table
Dan O'Neill: ran `ipvsadm -Ln` on gpu-pool-07 node: output shows 8 endpoints but 3 of them have zero active conns for long periods, weight=1 uniformly though
Mateo Ruiz: I dumped conntrack and saw many ESTABLISHED entries pinned to node gpu-nic-03 but ACKs retransmitted; tcpdump shows lots of dup ACKs and occasional ICMP frag needed
Alice Chen: MTU on some nodes is 1500, others 9000 — we recently rolled a kernel update with SR-IOV VF binding on some NICs, maybe fragmentation due to jumbo mismatch
Priya Kapoor: ohhh, we did enable mtu=9000 in the GPU ASG launch template last week for perf. Maybe older nodes still on 1500 and IPVS hashing sends flows unevenly
Dan O'Neill: also noticed RDMA (mlx5) verbs are bound on a subset. If RDMA/QP offload changes L4 path, ipvs might see different ports leading to skewed hash distribution
Alice Chen: reproduction steps I ran: curl against svc clusterIP from node A repeatedly; responses alternate between healthy pods and immediate resets when routed to certain endpoints
Mateo Ruiz: commands I ran: `kubectl get endpoints svc/gpu-infer -o wide` and `kubectl get pods -o wide` — some endpoints are NotReady briefly, but readiness probe is passing in pod logs
Priya Kapoor: could be asymmetric routing: replies leave via different node (B) with smaller MTU causing fragmentation and TCP stalls. If SYNs routed to node with jumbo but replies drop, retries happen
Dan O'Neill: quick check: `ip route show` on affected nodes shows different nexthop for the same pod CIDR because of a stale BGP adj in that AZ; that explains asymmetric egress
Alice Chen: mitigation idea: temporarily set kube-proxy mode to iptables or reduce ipvs persistent-ttl so connections remap faster? Also roll back MTU change on the ASG to 1500 until we can reconcile
Mateo Ruiz: iptables might increase CPU but quick toggle could prove if ipvs hashing is the issue
Priya Kapoor: I'll open a maintenance window to drain gpu-pool-07 and roll kernel/RF to unify MTU and unbind SR-IOV on a canary node
Dan O'Neill: meanwhile I added an annotation to the service to prefer local endpoints (externalTrafficPolicy: Local?) — wait that's for NodePort. Scratch that. But we can bias IPVS weight via endpoint controller (experimental)
infra-bot: incident created: INC-20260508-17 — assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20260508-17
Alice Chen: thanks — will collect more tcpdumps and ipvsadm saves and post next update. tagging @Priya @Mateo for the MTU/SDN change
Mateo Ruiz: also putting a temp alert to trigger if active connections on any endpoint drop to 0 while svc traffic remains high (to catch future skew early) :alarm_clock:
Priya Kapoor: plan: 1) canary node MTU rollback + disable SR-IOV VF 2) re-run ipvsadm/conntrack dumps 3) verify RDMA binding 4) if fixed, schedule wider roll 5) follow up with kernel vendor
Dan O'Neill: added note: we should validate kube-proxy version parity across nodes — we have 1.26 and 1.27 mixed clusters in eu-west2; ipvs behavior changed in 1.27 re: conn TTL
Alice Chen: ack. I'll grab kube-proxy logs and paste when done. Good catch everyone.
